overview: The single most fundamental split in bacteriology, driven entirely by cell wall architecture and visible with one classic stain.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: Bacteria with a thick peptidoglycan cell wall that retains crystal violet stain, appearing purple under the microscope after Gram staining.
aspects.valueB: Bacteria with a thin peptidoglycan layer and an outer membrane; they lose the crystal violet during decolorization and take up the safranin counterstain, appearing pink/red.

aspects.label: Cell Wall Structure
aspects.valueA: Thick peptidoglycan layer (multiple layers) with embedded teichoic and lipoteichoic acids; no outer membrane.
aspects.valueB: Thin peptidoglycan layer sandwiched between the plasma membrane and an outer membrane containing lipopolysaccharide (LPS).

aspects.label: Gram / Staining Reaction
aspects.valueA: Retains crystal violet-iodine complex through decolorization — stains purple.
aspects.valueB: Crystal violet-iodine complex washes out during decolorization; counterstained pink/red by safranin.

aspects.label: Growth Requirements
aspects.valueA: Varies widely by genus; many grow readily on standard nutrient media.
aspects.valueB: Varies widely by genus; some require selective/enriched media due to fastidious growth needs or LPS-related sensitivities.

aspects.label: Virulence Factors
aspects.valueA: Exotoxins are common; teichoic acids can contribute to immune activation.
aspects.valueB: LPS (endotoxin) in the outer membrane is a major virulence factor; some also produce exotoxins.

aspects.label: Identification
aspects.valueA: Gram stain morphology plus biochemical tests (e.g. catalase, coagulase) narrow genus/species.
aspects.valueB: Gram stain morphology plus biochemical/culture-based tests (e.g. oxidase, lactose fermentation) narrow genus/species.

aspects.label: Treatment Considerations
aspects.valueA: Often susceptible to antibiotics targeting peptidoglycan synthesis (e.g. many beta-lactams), though resistance mechanisms exist.
aspects.valueB: The outer membrane acts as an additional permeability barrier, affecting which antibiotics penetrate effectively; intrinsic resistance is common in several genera.

aspects.label: Limitations / Pitfalls
aspects.valueA: Old or damaged cells can over-decolorize and appear falsely Gram-negative.
aspects.valueB: Gram reaction alone does not identify species — it narrows a broad category, not a specific organism.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Thick peptidoglycan, no outer membrane, stains purple.
aspects.valueB: Thin peptidoglycan plus an LPS-containing outer membrane, stains pink/red.

aspects.label: Primary Purpose / Indication
aspects.valueA: First-line categorization step in identifying an unknown bacterial isolate.
aspects.valueB: First-line categorization step in identifying an unknown bacterial isolate.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Purple = positive = thick wall. Pink = negative = outer membrane with LPS.
overlay.memoryTrick: "Positive keeps its color, negative needs a new one."
overlay.commonMisconception: Gram-negative does not mean 'less dangerous' — LPS/endotoxin makes many Gram-negative infections especially serious.
